sub_scenario.family: night war-room leadership, dependency maps, and recovery debt
sub_scenario.one_line: network operations manager: decline and offer to lead the mapped daytime rollback review

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the topology map and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The on-call ledger review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I run a planned daylight maintenance bridge accurately from the topology map.
What does the map give you?
The upstream routing and authentication dependencies are visible at once.
Someone new shadowed me in the network bridge this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the maintenance nights into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For the metro routing outage, I marked the route reflectors and DNS edge on the topology before authorizing the rollback.
Did that prevent a mistake?
It kept us from restoring customer routes before name resolution was stable.
I can answer a routine alert-summary question late in the day.
Is that comparable to directing an outage?
No. A summary does not require committing a rollback sequence.
I archived last cycle's notes on the on-call ledger and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I am carrying recovery debt from a midnight fiber cut and a 04:00 maintenance page, so I am not taking another night command slot.
Could you sleep between them?
Not enough to be reliable by 22:30.
A vendor call about the topology map ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the network bridge checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the maintenance nights.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the on-call ledger records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
At the last uncharted BGP incident, I restarted the edge pair before the route reflector and extended the outage.
Why did that happen?
I had no current topology and was exhausted from the preceding maintenance window.
I sketched next week's plan for the maintenance nights before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the topology map updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My cardiologist asked me to avoid overnight energy drinks after an arrhythmia episode; a next-day deputy role is the safe alternative.
Can you lead briefly anyway?
Not when the decision window may run for hours.
I compared two options for the on-call ledger tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the network bridge handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I take the 22:30 Sev-1 bridge after the fiber-cut night?
